title: Caution: foreground depth can hide indispensable words

motion.summary: Cloaked figures occupy the foreground while the sons lyric sits behind their heads. Several sampled frames hide parts of the second line, demonstrating the cost of uncontrolled depth placement.
phases: Establish foreground silhouettes with small warm lanterns against a cool corridor.
Place text on a deeper plane, creating convincing overlap.
Observe the failure: heads cover letters needed to read the names.
motion.transferablePrinciple: Foreground overlap can make text inhabit a world, but the meaningful words require an unobstructed reading interval.
variations: Occlude only an already-read word during its departure.
Reserve a clear band above the silhouettes while allowing decorative type behind them.
Use a foreground passage to reveal, rather than continuously obscure, the crucial word.
cautions: Treat this as a cautionary example, not an approved legibility treatment.
Do not place names or essential lyric words behind opaque figures without a clear reading hold.
Review at phone size; small secondary verse text is already weak in this source.

quality.reviewer: agent visual inspection of decoded frame sequence
strengths: Warm lanterns and cool silhouettes establish strong depth and atmosphere.
The reference exposes a concrete compositing failure useful for future reviews.
limitations: Important letters in the sons line are visibly hidden across several samples.
The small lower verse line has weak contrast and is difficult to read.
Observed from six decoded frames of the exact hashed MP4; this is a concept reference, not full motion, audio-sync or whole-film acceptance.
